fatal_errors: The proposed intervention omits the governing HEBM–SPS processing pathway and its controlled milling and sintering parameters.
The experiment varies both composition and processing, so it cannot isolate short-range order as the cause of mechanical-property changes.
The cited evidence does not support the predicted 10–20% strengthening or the arbitrary 5% falsification threshold.
The stated boundary of ambient temperature and pressure is not a meaningful applicability limit for a hypothesis based on processing-induced chemical order.
explanation: Short-range order and chemical heterogeneity are scientifically plausible contributors to dislocation resistance in some concentrated alloys, and E3 provides relevant evidence linking heat-treatment-induced order to changed slip behavior. However, this does not reconstruct the target CoCrFeNiTi mechanism, which depends on high-energy ball milling, nanocrystalline grain refinement, accumulated lattice strain/dislocations, solid-solution strengthening, densification, and an FCC/BCC phase mixture produced by SPS. No milling duration, speed, ball-to-powder ratio, SPS temperature, heating rate, phase fraction, grain size, density, or target mechanical values are recovered. The baseline is only loosely aligned because it mentions as-cast material but does not specify its porosity and heterogeneity. The proposed comparison is heavily confounded, and tensile testing alone does not directly quantify short-range order. A discriminating test would hold composition, grain size, phase fraction, density, and defect density constant while changing only thermal histories that alter short-range order, then correlate direct SRO measurements with hardness and strength.
